title: StarterCraft: Pocket onramp guide and 45m integrator flow (draft)
content:
Why this exists:
A tiny, portable quickstart and workshop flow for integrators to get from zero to an instrumented sample app in 45 minutes. Focus is on first-success rituals, observable checks, and a minimal failure triage path. Intended to be used by Developer Advocates, Solutions Eng, and internal SDK folks during 1:1 sessions and short workshops.

Audience:
- Engineers who need a fast way to evaluate Redwood SDKs and runtime behavior
- Solutions engineers doing a 30–60 minute discovery call
- Internal advocates running hands-on demos

Success criteria (what ‘done’ looks like):
- Participant can make an authenticated request and read a streaming response within 10 minutes.
- Telemetry (latency, tokens, error rate) shows up in console/telemetry within 20 minutes.
- One simple fallback implemented (client-side retry or alternative model route) by end of session.

Quick 10-minute lift (for live demos) — top-level steps:
1) Pre-reqs: account with API key, node 18+/python3.10, Docker optional.
2) Clone tiny-sample-app repo (link provided in linked_artifacts).
3) Set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var.
4) Run one-liner smoke: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"model":"synth-1","input":"Hello from StarterCraft"}'
   - Expected: 200 + streaming chunk(s). If plaintext error, look for 401/429/5xx.
5) Open Console -> Telemetry -> Requests and watch the sample request appear (filter by token or path).

45-minute workshop flow (timed):
- 0–5m: Intros + objective (set expectations: demo + hands-on)
- 5–15m: Quick key setup + smoke curl (walk through auth errors)
- 15–25m: Run sample server (node/python) and call SDK streaming path, highlight retry/backoff hooks
- 25–35m: Add one telemetry breakpoint (log token cost + latency) and push a tiny change to show incremental feedback in console
- 35–40m: Introduce fallback: switch to smaller model or alternate region; show routing policy change in request header
- 40–45m: Wrap, next steps, collect issues/feedback

Minimal code snippets (plain text for copy/paste):
- Node (tiny example):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  (async () => {
    const stream = client.generate({ model: 'synth-1', input: 'Summarize this email' });
    for await (const chunk of stream) console.log(chunk.text);
  })().catch(e => console.error('sample error', e));

- Python (sync-ish):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
  resp = client.generate(model='synth-1', input='Explain Redis caching in one sentence')
  print(resp.text)

Telemetry & instrumentation checklist (must-have for workshop):
- Console: request appears within 2 minutes of call
- Telemetry tags: sdk_version, sample-id, workshop-run
- Token metrics: per-request token count + topk usage visible
- Latency: p50/p95 visible after ~10 calls
- Error logs: include full request-id (for support escalation)
- Basic alert/threshold set locally: error_rate > 5% or p95 > 2s -> note for follow-up

Common failure modes and triage heuristics (notes-to-self style):
- 401 unauthorized: check REDWOOD_API_KEY, whitespace paste errors, org-level access. Quick fix: regen key in console and try.
- 429 rate limit: reduce concurrency, demonstrate 'retry-with-jitter' snippet, file GH issue if reproducible.
- Streaming hang: check network proxies, confirm content-length vs chunked; enable client debug logs and capture request-id.
- Model mismatch / incompatible payload: show example of schema validation error and quick mapping to request body.

Minimal fallback patterns to teach (one-liners to copy):
- Client side: exponentialBackoff(retries=3) wrapper around client.generate
- Routing header: x-redwood-model: synth-1-compact -> demonstrate cost/latency tradeoff in console

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should StarterCraft include a templated prompt suite for prompt-regression checks? (ENG-1289)
- Add a lightweight GitHub Actions workflow that runs the smoke curl and verifies Telemetry ingestion -> low friction CI.
- Decide on official sample model name (synth-1 used here as placeholder).
- Create a 5-minute video snippet for self-serve onboarding (host on drive).

Next steps (short backlog):
- [ ] Finalize sample repos: combine node/python into single mono-repo (owner: Ben)
- [ ] Add GH action smoke test (owner: Rafael)
- [ ] Draft 5-min demo video and slide 1-liner (owner: Sofia)
- [ ] Wire a one-click sandbox button (console) to pre-provision sample API key & telemetry tag (product ask)

Notes to facilitator:
- Keep it interactive: ask participants to paste their curl output into chat if on remote call.
- If network weirdness happens, switch to recorded run and show logs (have a recorded trace ready).
- Measure success by whether at least one participant sees their request in Console -> Telemetry during the session.

Quick links (for facilitator use during session):
- Sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/startercraft-sample
- Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEV/StarterCraft+Playbook
- Support escalation: internal Slack #devexp-support, include request-id when filing

End of draft — this is intentionally readable as a single-page handout. Keep feedback granular (what was confusing, what failed for you, what would you want automated next time).
summary: Draft pocket guide to onboard engineers through a 45m hands-on SDK + telemetry workshop: smoke commands, snippets, triage heuristics, and small backlog.
